subproblem.title: Bound scalar evaluation by homogeneous coefficients
subproblem.statement: Let n∈ℕ, R∈BinaryForm ℂ n, z∈ℂ, and b∈ℝ with b≥0. Suppose every monomial coefficient of R has absolute value at most b. Then |R(1,−z)|≤(n+1)max(1,|z|)^n b.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (R : ↥(HeckeEis.BinaryForm ℂ n)) (z : ℂ) (b : ℝ), 0 ≤ b → (∀ d : Fin 2 →₀ ℕ, ‖MvPolynomial.coeff d R.val‖ ≤ b) → ‖MvPolynomial.eval (fun j : Fin 2 => if j = 0 then 1 else -z) R.val‖ ≤ ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * (max 1 ‖z‖) ^ n * b
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Homogeneity means that a nonzero coefficient can occur only at an exponent pair whose sum is n. Such pairs are exactly (r,n−r), with 0≤r≤n. Hence R(X,Y)=Σ_{r=0}^n c_r X^rY^(n−r), where each c_r is a monomial coefficient of R and satisfies |c_r|≤b.
2. Evaluate at X=1 and Y=−z to obtain R(1,−z)=Σ_{r=0}^n c_r(−z)^(n−r). The triangle inequality and multiplicativity of the complex norm give |R(1,−z)|≤Σ_{r=0}^n |c_r||z|^(n−r).
3. Set M=max(1,|z|). Then M≥1 and |z|≤M. Since 0≤n−r≤n, one has |z|^(n−r)≤M^(n−r)≤M^n. Each summand in step 2 is therefore at most bM^n, using b≥0.
4. There are exactly n+1 summands. Their sum is at most (n+1)bM^n=(n+1)M^n b, which is the claimed bound. For n=0 this argument has one summand and M^0=1, so it covers that case as well.
proof_key_steps: Enumerate the n+1 possible degree-n monomials.
Expand evaluation at (1,−z) and apply the triangle inequality.
Bound every monomial evaluation by max(1,|z|)^n.

audit.reason: The exact proposition evaluates the Fin 2 variables at (1,−z), includes b≥0 and every coefficient bound, and uses the correct real-valued factor n+1. The proof enumerates the n+1 homogeneous monomials, applies the triangle inequality, bounds each power by max(1,‖z‖)^n, and sums. It covers n=0 without additional assumptions. The obligation is non-circular and its bare identifier is unreserved.
